title: Promise and Songbook
premise: Marine biologist Sable Villalobos has spent a decade training her heart into submission after her family's orchard burned and her first love, Marisol Ferre, vanished with the deed. When a probate error names both women co-owners of the surviving vineyard block, Sable returns to the valley intending to sell fast and leave faster. But Marisol, now a luthier who builds instruments from the orchard's dead trees, is determined to see one harvest through, and the town that raised them both closes ranks around the land. As grafting season becomes harvest season, Sable must choose between a prestigious post abroad and the woman who taught her that memory, like a vine, can be pruned without being killed. She stays — not for the deed, but because love, she finally admits, was never a muscle to contain.
about_author: Sebastian Thackeray is a former agricultural extension agent who spent twelve years cataloguing heirloom orchards across the Pacific coast before turning to fiction. He writes romances rooted in working landscapes, where land records and labor carry as much weight as longing.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A probate clerk's letter arrives at Sable's coastal lab naming her and Marisol Ferre as co-owners of the Villalobos vineyard block — the same Marisol who disappeared eleven years ago. Sable drafts a refusal, then burns it in the sink. Emotional beat: dread sharpened by an old wound reopening.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable arrives in the valley planning a two-day trip: assess, list, sell. The town greets her like someone who never left, and she learns Marisol has been living in the old packing house, building guitars from fire-killed trees. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay archived.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left Standing
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol watches Sable measure the vines for a buyer's report and confronts her with the truth of why she left — a letter Sable never sent, a father's ultimatum neither fully understood. They agree, coldly, to split the season: ninety days to harvest, then the sale. Emotional beat: brittle truce over shared grief.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Forced to work the block together, they fall into old rhythms — dawn irrigation, Marisol's hands teaching Sable graft cuts. Sable's career rival emails about the overseas post; Marisol finds the unsent letter hidden in a guitar's soundboard. Emotional beat: tenderness leaking through professional armor.

chapters.title: The Found Family Table
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The town's Sunday dinners at the orchard swell into something like a household: the retired foreman, Marisol's apprentice, Sable's old lab assistant who shows up unannounced. Sable realizes she has been lonely in a way data never measured. Emotional beat: belonging arriving uninvited and undeniable.

chapters.title: Powdery Mildew
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Disease strikes the vines weeks before harvest; the buyer's offer shrinks. Sable works herself hollow saving the crop while hiding the acceptance letter for the overseas post. Marisol finds it, says nothing, and starts varnishing a guitar she won't explain. Emotional beat: quiet betrayal before any crime is committed.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Harvest eve. The grapes come in beautiful against all odds, and the town throws a festival under strung lights. Sable and Marisol nearly kiss among the crush bins — then Sable's flight confirmation buzzes on the table between them. Emotional beat: joy cresting directly into rupture.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Soundboard
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol finishes the guitar built from the burned orchard's last tree and gives it to Sable with the eleven-year-old letter inside — proof she never stopped choosing her. Sable, cornered by duty and terror, boards her flight anyway. Emotional beat: heartbreak with the door deliberately left open.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Mid-Atlantic, Sable opens the guitar case and reads the letter at last, then watches the ocean she studies and understands it holds no one waiting for her. She turns the ship around at the next port, resigns the post, and drives through the night back to the valley. Emotional beat: the contained heart finally breaking open on purpose.

chapters.title: Promise and Songbook
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Sable arrives during the first pressing, grape-stained and certain. She and Marisol tear up the sale contract, register the deed jointly in both their names, and play the orchard-wood guitar at the harvest table surrounded by their found family. Emotional beat: resolution — love chosen over duty, memory kept alive by making something new from what survived.
